mainTopic: Does רבי עקיבא hold that a person can transfer or forbid something that does not exist yet (דבר שלא בא לעולם)? A proof from the vow 'קונם whatever I make for your mouth', a rejection of that proof, and a chain of rabbis showing that רבי עקיבא does allow it.
overview: The גמרא brings a משנה about a wife who uses a נדר to forbid her future earnings to her husband. The first opinion says the husband does not need to annul it. רבי עקיבא says he should annul it, which seems to show that a נדר can take hold on things that do not exist yet. The גמרא rejects this proof: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע explains that she vowed on her hands, which already exist. The גמרא then notes that this conflicts with רב נחמן בר יצחק. He traces a chain of rabbis, from רב הונא back to רבי עקיבא, who all hold 'אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם'. The גמרא then shows the source for each name. For רב הונא it is his ruling on selling palm fruit before it grows, and רב נחמן disagrees with that ruling. For רב it is giving away a field before buying it. For רבי ינאי and רבי חייא it is a story about separating מעשר for fruit that had not arrived yet. רבי חייא supports his ruling with a ברייתא about 'all the days', and the גמרא begins working out what law that ברייתא teaches. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The vow on future earnings: the first opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a משנה about a wife who forbids to her husband whatever she will make. The first opinion says he does not need to annul it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a wife says 'קונם, whatever I make for your mouth,' the husband does not need to annul the vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof by quoting the first half of a משנה. The proof itself comes in the next line, from רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife already owes her earnings to her husband as part of the marriage, so her נדר has nothing to take hold on. Because of that, the first opinion says the husband does not need to do anything.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow word: 'this is forbidden like a קרבן'
To annul a vow (הפרה), which a husband can do for his wife
A wife's earnings, which belong to her husband

phrases.english: Konam: whatever I make for your mouth
phrases.notes: Literally 'for your mouth.' She means the earnings from her work, which would feed him.

phrases.english: he does not need to annul it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the proof by citing the first opinion in the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי עקיבא holds that a person can act on something that does not exist yet.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about 'קונם שאני עושה לפיך'.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא says the husband should annul
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says the husband should annul the vow, in case she earns more than he is entitled to. That suggests a נדר can take hold on earnings that do not exist yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: He should annul it, because she might produce more for him than he is entitled to.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the heart of the proof. רבי עקיבא worries the vow could take hold on her extra earnings, even though those earnings do not exist yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband is only entitled to a set amount of her earnings. Anything beyond that would fall under the vow. Those future earnings are a דבר שלא בא לעולם, so it seems רבי עקיבא holds that a vow can take hold on something not yet in existence.

keyTerms.meaning: He should annul (the vow)
She will produce extra, more than required
What he is properly entitled to

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: He should annul it,
lest she produce extra for him,
more than what is due to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second opinion in the משנה, which is where the proof comes from.
steps.raayaObject: רבי עקיבא holds that a vow or transfer can take hold on a דבר שלא בא לעולם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's worry about her extra future earnings, which do not exist yet.

steps.title: Rejecting the proof: she vowed on her hands
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע explains that the משנה is about a woman who forbids her hands, which already exist. So there is no proof about things that do not exist yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it said about this משנה by רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: it is about a woman who says 'Let my hands be holy to their Maker.' Hands exist in the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof. It explains the משנה differently, so that the vow is on something that already exists: her hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she forbade her hands themselves, then the vow takes hold on a real, existing object, and whatever her hands produce is forbidden through them. That removes the case from דבר שלא בא לעולם, so the משנה tells us nothing about רבי עקיבא's view on that question.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But it was already said about it': introduces an earlier explanation
'Let my hands be holy to their Maker'
They exist in the world

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not rejected because רבי עקיבא's words are changed. It is rejected because the case is read as a vow on her hands, which exist, instead of a vow on future earnings.

phrases.english: But wasn't it stated about it:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
it is a case where she says: 'Let my hands be holy to their Maker,'
since hands exist in the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from steps 1-2 by reading the משנה's case differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely. The משנה is no longer about something that does not exist yet.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed she vowed on future earnings. In fact she vowed on her hands, which already exist.

steps.title: A chain of rabbis back to רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this reading disagrees with רב נחמן בר יצחק. He traces רב הונא's view through a chain of rabbis back to רבי עקיבא, who says a person can transfer something that does not exist yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with רב נחמן בר יצחק, who said: רב הונא follows רב, רב follows רבי ינאי, רבי ינאי follows רבי חייא, רבי חייא follows רבי, רבי follows רבי מאיר, רבי מאיר follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב follows רבי עקיבא, who said: A person can transfer something that has not yet come into the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a disagreement. רב נחמן בר יצחק holds that רבי עקיבא does allow transferring something that does not exist yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rejection in step 3 suggested that רבי עקיבא might not allow a דבר שלא בא לעולם. רב נחמן בר יצחק says clearly that he does, and links a whole line of rabbis to that view. So the two approaches to רבי עקיבא's position conflict.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it disagrees with...'
A person can transfer ownership
Something that has not yet come into existence

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן בר יצחק, רבי עקיבא holds 'אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם', and a long chain of rabbis follows him. This conflicts with the reading of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether a person can transfer or forbid something that does not exist yet is a major question across many areas of הלכה. Here the גמרא shows that רבי עקיבא's view is the root of a whole line of opinions.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak.
For Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא כְּרַב, וְרַב כְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי,
phrases.english: Rav Huna follows Rav, and Rav follows Rabbi Yannai,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יַנַּאי כְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא, וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא כְּרַבִּי,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yannai follows Rabbi Chiya, and Rabbi Chiya follows Rabbi,
phrases.notes: Plain 'רבי' here means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: and Rabbi follows Rabbi Meir,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Meir follows Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov follows Rabbi Akiva,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: אָדָם מַקְנֶה דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: who said: A person can transfer something that has not yet come into the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Notes that the rejection in step 3 conflicts with רב נחמן בר יצחק's statement about רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא holds 'אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם', and רב הונא, רב, רבי ינאי, רבי חייא, רבי, רבי מאיר, and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב all follow him.

steps.title: רב הונא's source: selling palm-tree fruit before it grows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רב הונא's view comes from. It answers with his ruling on selling palm fruit: before the fruit grows the seller can back out, but once it grows he cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we see רב הונא's view? It was taught: if someone sells the fruit of a palm tree to his friend, רב הונא said that before the fruit comes into the world, the seller can back out. Once it comes into the world, he can no longer back out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts going through the names in רב נחמן בר יצחק's chain. It shows the ruling of רב הונא that proves he holds a person can transfer something that does not exist yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the sale was made, the fruit did not exist. Even so, רב הונא says the sale locks in once the fruit appears, with no new act of acquisition needed. So a sale of something not yet in existence can take effect once that thing exists.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? Here it means: where is this opinion found?
As it was stated (introduces a teaching of the אמוראים)
One who sells
The fruit of a palm tree
To back out of the deal

phrases.english: Rav Huna, what is it?
phrases.notes: He means: where do we see that רב הונא is on the list from step 4?

phrases.english: As it was stated:
One who sells the fruit of a palm tree to his fellow,
Rav Huna said:
Until they have come into the world,
he can back out.
Once they have come into the world,
he cannot back out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins showing the source for the first name in רב נחמן בר יצחק's chain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sale of palm fruit that has not grown yet becomes final once the fruit appears, so the seller can no longer back out.

steps.title: רב נחמן disagrees: the seller can back out even after the fruit grows
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the seller can back out even after the fruit has grown.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: even after the fruit comes into the world, the seller can still back out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן argues with רב הונא about the palm-fruit sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב נחמן, the fruit growing later does not fix the sale. The sale was made when the fruit did not exist, so it never fully took hold. That shows he holds a person cannot transfer something that does not exist yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Even
Once they have come into the world (once they exist)
Is able, can

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said:
Even once they have come into the world,
he can back out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רב הונא's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The seller of fruit that has not grown yet can back out even after the fruit appears.

steps.title: רב נחמן admits: if the buyer already ate, we don't take it back
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן agrees that if the buyer grabbed the fruit and ate it, בית דין does not make him pay it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: I admit that if the buyer grabbed the fruit and ate it, we do not take it away from him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן adds a limit to his own ruling. He concedes one practical point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though רב נחמן says the sale is not binding, he does not let the seller take back fruit the buyer has already eaten. So the seller can stop the deal, but he cannot undo what already happened.

keyTerms.meaning: I admit, I agree
Grabs, snatches
And eats
We do not take it out of his hands

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
I admit that if he grabs and eats,
phrases.notes: The one who grabs and eats is the buyer, taking the fruit he paid for.

phrases.english: we do not take it away from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב נחמן's own ruling from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the buyer has already taken and eaten the fruit, בית דין does not take it from him.

steps.title: רב's source: giving away a field before buying it
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a person can give his friend a field he is about to buy, starting from the moment he buys it, and the friend acquires it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we see רב's view? רב הונא said in the name of רב: if someone tells his friend, 'This field that I am going to buy, once I buy it, it is yours from now,' the friend acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next name on the list, רב. It brings his ruling about a field the speaker does not own yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he speaks, the field is not his, so he is handing over something he does not have yet. רב says the transfer works anyway. That shows רב holds a person can transfer something that has not come into his hands.

keyTerms.meaning: When I buy it
It is acquired by you, it is yours
From now
He has acquired it

phrases.english: Rav:
phrases.notes: The words 'what is his source?' are understood here, just as with רב הונא in step 5.

phrases.english: As Rav Huna said that Rav said:
One who says to his fellow:
'This field that I am buying,'
'when I buy it,'
'it is acquired by you from now,'
he has acquired it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב — דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רב הונא to the next name in the chain, רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person can transfer a field he has not bought yet, and the transfer takes effect once he buys it.

steps.title: רבי ינאי's sharecropper is late, and he asks רבי חייא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי ינאי holds like רבי חייא through a story. רבי ינאי separated מעשר for fruit that had not reached him yet, and then went to ask רבי חייא about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי holds like רבי חייא. רבי ינאי had a sharecropper who used to bring him a basket of fruit every ערב שבת. One day the sharecropper was late and had not come. רבי ינאי took מעשר from the fruit in his house to cover that fruit. He then came before רבי חייא...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts telling a story to show that רבי ינאי and רבי חייא share the same view. רבי חייא's answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי separated מעשר for fruit that was not yet in his hands. If that works, it means something not yet in a person's possession can be dealt with now. רבי חייא's answer, which comes next, will show what both of them hold.

keyTerms.meaning: A sharecropper, who works the owner's field for a share of the crop
A basket
ערב שבת, Friday
It got late for him, he was late
Separated מעשר (tithe)
Before him, in front of him

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai is like Rabbi Chiya:
phrases.notes: He means: רבי ינאי's place on the list is shown through a story with רבי חייא.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yannai had a sharecropper
who would bring him
a basket of fruit
every Shabbat eve.
One day he was late
and did not come.
He took and tithed from the fruit of his house for them.
phrases.notes: 'For them' means for the fruit the sharecropper had not brought yet.

phrases.english: He came before Rabbi Chiya,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַנַּאי כְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא — דְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי הֲוָה לֵיהּ אֲרִיסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next names in the chain, רבי ינאי and רבי חייא, through a story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only: רבי ינאי separated מעשר for fruit not yet in his hands and went to ask רבי חייא. The ruling comes next.

steps.title: רבי חייא approves what רבי ינאי did
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא answers רבי ינאי's question by telling him he acted well.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You did well.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי had separated מעשר for fruit that had not reached him yet and came to ask about it. רבי חייא answers that he did the right thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the payoff of the story from step 9. רבי חייא approves of separating מעשר ahead of time for fruit that has not arrived, and this shows that רבי ינאי's practice matches רבי חייא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: You acted well / you did the right thing
He said to him

phrases.english: He said to him: You acted well.
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבי חייא, answering רבי ינאי from the story just before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי חייא's answer to the question רבי ינאי brought in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי ינאי was right to separate מעשר for fruit that had not yet reached him.

steps.title: A ברייתא reads "all the days" as including שבת and יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא supports his answer with a ברייתא that reads "כׇּל הַיָּמִים" in the פסוק about מעשר as including שבתות and ימים טובים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: "So that you learn to fear ה׳ your God all the days". These are שבתות and ימים טובים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא brings a ברייתא as a source for why רבי ינאי acted well. The ברייתא says the word "all" in this פסוק about מעשר comes to include שבת and יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about eating מעשר. The ברייתא learns from the extra word "כׇּל" that the פסוק also covers שבתות and ימים טובים. At this point we are not yet told what law this teaches, so the גמרא will ask about that next.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
All the days. The extra word "all" is read as including more days
שבתות and holidays

phrases.english: As it is taught: "So that you learn to fear
phrases.notes: דברים 14:23. This פסוק is about eating מעשר.

phrases.english: ה׳ your God all the days"
These are שבתות and holidays.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא learns this from the word "all": even these special days are included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind רבי חייא's approval in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חייא's approval of רבי ינאי's early separation of מעשר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading "כׇּל הַיָּמִים" in דברים 14:23 as including שבתות and ימים טובים.

steps.title: What law does the ברייתא teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical law comes from including שבתות and ימים טובים in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law was this said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what practical point the ברייתא is making. This question sets up the next move, where the גמרא tries out possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said "all the days" includes שבת and יום טוב, but it did not say what you may or must do on those days. The גמרא needs to pin this down to understand how the ברייתא supports רבי ינאי.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? What is the practical point?

phrases.english: For what law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what practical law the ברייתא quoted in step 11 is teaching.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical law taught by including שבתות and ימים טובים in the פסוק about מעשר.

steps.title: It cannot mean permission to separate מעשר and eat on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא means one may separate מעשר and eat on שבת. It rejects this, because a פסוק would not be needed to permit טלטול, which is only forbidden מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means one may separate מעשר and eat on שבת, would a פסוק be needed to permit טלטול, which is only a rabbinic prohibition?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one answer: the ברייתא permits separating מעשר and eating on שבת. It immediately pushes this answer away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only problem the גמרא raises with doing this on שבת is טלטול, moving things, and that is forbidden only by the רבנן. The Torah would not need a פסוק to permit something that is forbidden only מדרבנן. So the ברייתא must be teaching something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say. This introduces a suggested answer that will be tested
To separate מעשר and eat
Moving objects on שבת
Forbidden by the רבנן, not by the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: The ending "?!" is not a real question. It means "Of course a פסוק is not needed for that!" It rejects the suggested answer.

phrases.english: If you say: to separate מעשר and eat,
phrases.notes: He means separating מעשר and eating on שבת or יום טוב.

phrases.english: Was a verse needed to permit moving objects, which is only rabbinic?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries a first answer to the question in step 12 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the ברייתא as permission to separate מעשר and eat on שבת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The only problem the גמרא raises is טלטול, which is forbidden only מדרבנן, and the Torah does not need a פסוק to permit a rabbinic prohibition.
